# Single-fluid KRAKEN and KRAKENC reference artifacts

Generated by Acoustics Toolbox v2023.5, commit
`475108519289c6fb488b58980c644ea14eccc604`, not by Rust. The pinned
`tools/reference/Dockerfile` uses Linux x86-64, GNU Fortran 12.2.0
(Debian 12.2.0-14+deb12u1), and
`-O1 -ffast-math -funroll-all-loops -fomit-frame-pointer -std=gnu`.

`PekerisBroadband.env` derives from Pekeris by changing the title, adding
`B` in the sixth top-option slot, selecting `W` loss and 0.8 dB/wavelength
bottom attenuation, NG 1000→101, RMax 2→1000 km, and appending three
frequencies in the order 75/50/62.5 Hz. Its `.flp` changes only the title.
`PekerisComplexBroadband` changes only the title and cHigh 1700→2000 m/s.
Both use mesh multipliers 1/2/4: at 75 Hz the intervals are 151/303/606,
at 50 Hz 101/202/404, and at 62.5 Hz 126/252/505. Three pinned runs per
pair yield identical `.mod/.shd` binaries. Committed and fresh comparisons
check all frequencies, with 5/3/4 KRAKEN or 7/4/6 KRAKENC modes and nine
line-source pressures per frequency. **They are derived inputs, not the
original BroadBand/MunkK.**

The **unmodified upstream** `tests/BroadBand/MunkK.env/.flp` is separately
compared through **KRAKEN** in fresh pinned CI at 50/500 Hz: 102/1,023 modes and 501,501 pressures
per frequency (1,003,002 total). Input SHA-256 is respectively
`9ccab68c7ace7525904e6761d52056dc141fb4e1ca6c43929c86e9a22b5986c9` /
`97e8d768e3b7e48948539913f56b2dd5dfc71406bfeef49271bf63209912588f`.
Three runs yielded identical `.mod/.shd` SHA-256
`58d9ea25379bce98f17c5b59c7ffd3e9680984fadc8ee8bc59daeaacbdcfb4e3` /
`6cd0811cc1985fb70a78e3ac510dfd7b501a7cff21208cd7ea66be339d65ba20`.
Original binaries stay out of Git. This pair differs from the original
single-frequency `tests/Munk/MunkK`, which remains a separate regression.

`PekerisComplex.env` derives from Pekeris by enabling KRAKENC restarts
(`NVN .`), raising cHigh from 1700 to 2000 m/s, and setting RMax to 0.
`PekerisComplexBlank` changes only the restart option to the valid default
`NVN`; the pinned Fortran modal table and binary equal PekerisComplex, so its
offline test reuses those goldens, while fresh CI runs both inputs separately.
`PekerisComplexSlow` changes only the bottom speed from 1700 to 1400 m/s;
its four modes all radiate into the bottom and have their own `.mod/.prt`.
`PekerisComplexCLow` changes the blank-restart case's cLow from 1400 to
1550 m/s: its first mode is out of band, while the remaining three have their
own `.mod/.prt`. The blank setting produces a stable three-mode v2023.5
reference; Fortran's dotted random-restart option sometimes also emits the
out-of-band mode for this input, so that variant is not a reproducible oracle.
`PekerisComplexRefined.env` derives from PekerisComplexBlank by changing the
title, NG 1000→100 and RMax 0→1000 km; its `.flp` changes only the title. The
pinned solver uses mesh multipliers 1/2/4. Three runs produced identical
`.mod/.shd` binaries; all four modes and nine pressures match the committed
goldens and fresh CI.
`PekerisComplexBlank.flp` is a **separately derived** coherent line-source FIELD
input with nine pressures. Its committed `.shd` binary matches a second pinned
Fortran run; its `.mod` binary is unchanged and reuses the PekerisComplex
modes golden.
`PekerisComplexGradient` changes only the 100 m water SSP point from 1500 to
1520 m/s relative to PekerisComplexBlank; `PekerisComplexReverseGradient`
reverses that 1500→1520 m/s gradient. Pinned Fortran blank-restart runs
returned identical `.mod` binaries three times per case; their own `.mod/.prt`
check all four modes including one leaky mode each. Both are **derived**, not
original MunkKleaky or sduct inputs.
`MunkLeakyPartial.env` starts from upstream `tests/MunkLeaky/MunkKleaky.env`
(SHA-256 `176a4e2f9c3b142d9f58c2fc691374a789b470322bfd44eb5679da754604e60a`).
It retains exactly the first seven water SSP records (0–1000 m) and the 50 Hz
frequency, bottom speed/density and `RMax=0`; changes the title, depth
5000→1000 m, NG 5000→800, `NVW .`→`NVN` (blank restarts), bottom attenuation
0.8→0 dB/wavelength, cHigh 20000→1700 m/s, and source/receiver mode-sampling
depths. `MunkLeakyPartialLoss` changes only the derived bottom attenuation
from 0 to the original 0.8 dB/wavelength `W` loss. Three pinned Fortran runs
per derived case yielded identical `.mod` binaries: 30 modes, nine leaky each.
A **separately derived** coherent point-source `MunkLeakyPartialLoss.flp`
selects two source depths, six receiver depths, three ranges (including zero)
and nonnegative offsets; the original `.env`-derived modal sampling grid is
unchanged. Three pinned Fortran runs yielded identical `.mod` and `.shd`
binaries; 36 complex pressures match a committed `.shd` golden and fresh CI.
`MunkLeakyPartialC.env` changes only `N`→`C` relative to the lossy derivative;
its separately derived `.flp` changes only the title. Three pinned runs
produced identical `.mod/.shd` binaries (30 modes, nine leaky; 36 pressures)
and all samples match committed goldens and fresh CI. **These are derived
inputs, not original MunkKwb/Kbb or sductK examples.**
The **unmodified upstream** `MunkKleaky.env` (same SHA above) and `.flp`
(SHA-256 `72b6e29b05b048bf8fc5dc67559ba1c037ff8f82455e93d83ce81777f207e4e6`)
are separately compared with fresh pinned Fortran in CI: 329 complex modes,
every mode sample, attenuation, group speed and all 150,801 complex pressures.
Three local pinned Fortran runs of the original pair produced identical `.mod`
and `.shd` binaries. The `.env` determines modal samples; the original `.flp`
provides FIELD geometry. Four other **unmodified** pairs are compared in
fresh pinned CI: `MunkKwb.env/.flp` (63 modes, 150,801 pressures),
`MunkKbb.env/.flp` (102, 150,801), `sductK.env/.flp` (1,077, 201,201) and
`calibK.env/.flp` (33, 101,101; mesh multipliers 1/2/4).
Their SHA-256 input pairs are respectively

The final pair is upstream `tests/calib/calibK`; the preceding three use the

binaries. No original `.mod/.shd` binary is committed.
A 10,000× depth / 10,000× inverse-frequency scaling of `PekerisComplex` is
tested metamorphically against the original modes to guard root separation;
it is **not** claimed as a fresh Fortran acceptance (the pinned solver returns
only three modes with blank restarts and has variable small imaginary roundoff
with dotted restarts at that scale).
The remaining **derived inputs** have no `.flp` or FIELD goldens: modes-only
tests use `Pekeris.flp` solely for valid geometry; the `.env` determines modal
sampling depths. The pinned `krakenc-fortran` reference produces `.mod/.prt`
and FIELD produces `.shd` for four single-frequency derived fixtures, the
broadband Pekeris derivative and five original pairs; committed binaries are
unmodified and `.prt` files have trailing spaces removed. The same comparator
checks all ten single-frequency derived cases, the broadband derivative and
five original pairs in fresh CI, including every complex32 wavenumber, phase-aligned shape,
print precision and attenuation. It also checks every complex pressure for
all five derived FIELD fixtures and five original pairs. These acceptances do not
imply general KRAKENC FIELD support outside the coherent single-profile subset.
`PekerisRigid`/`PekerisRigidLoss` change only the surface from `V` to `R`
(relative to Pekeris/PekerisDenseLoss respectively) and use distinct titles.
They are **derived fixtures**, not unmodified upstream examples.
`PekerisHard` and `PekerisHardBoth` derive from PekerisSpline3, replace the
acoustic bottom record with a rigid condition (and `cHigh=2000` m/s), and
exercise vacuum/rigid surfaces respectively. They are **not** official inputs.
`PekerisRigidPlane` is another **derived input**, constructed for the exact
rigid-rigid plane-mode endpoint; it is not an upstream example. Its 17-point
base mesh and refined meshes keep the same two Fortran modes.
`MunkLossless` replaces `NVW` with `NVN`, bottom loss `0.8` with `0`,
and limits receiver/mode/field grids. `MunkBottomLoss` retains the upstream
loss and profile but also reduces the grids (not an original upstream input).
`MunkAnalytic.env` changes the original `tests/Munk/MunkAnalytic.env` title,
mesh count (0 → 2000), and RMax (200 → 0 km); its `.flp` is a new coherent
line-source FIELD input. The original `.env` SHA-256 is
`3cc2a2121d9ae3ff395fc138ef31656f907f09d57a195fd9bdda77f42bf37162`.
It is **derived**, not a comparison of the unmodified official pair. The
original auto-mesh/extrapolated **`.env`** is separately compared in CI
against fresh Fortran `.mod/.prt` with a derived coherent FIELD `.flp`, under
the same exact complex32 `.mod` check. The original three-line `.flp` cannot
be parsed by the pinned v2023.5 FIELD; it is not an accepted original pair.
The sduct-derived inputs restrict cHigh from 100000 m/s to the 1523.9 m/s
bottom speed and limit the coordinate grids. `SductTrapped` replaces `CVW`
with `CVN`; `SductPchip` uses `PVW` and explicitly specifies 0.8 dB/wavelength
bottom loss; `SductSpline` uses lossless `SVN`. These are **not** comparisons
to the unmodified official examples. **CI separately compares the unmodified upstream MunkK
`.env/.flp` end to end** (102 modes, 501,501 pressure samples) against the pinned
Fortran output, plus the unmodified MunkAnalytic `.env` with separately derived
coherent FIELD input (102 modes, 25 pressure samples). Unmodified sductK is separately compared end-to-end via KRAKENC, not KRAKEN.
`tests/PekerisRD` upstream is a BELLHOP case, not a KRAKEN oracle.

Re-run fresh numerical comparisons from the repository root:

```sh
for case in Pekeris PekerisFiltered PekerisDense PekerisDenseLoss PekerisRefined PekerisSpline3 PekerisRigid PekerisRigidLoss PekerisHard PekerisHardBoth PekerisRigidPlane MunkLossless MunkBottomLoss MunkAnalytic SductTrapped SductPchip SductSpline; do
  tools/reference/compare-kraken.sh "crates/kraken/tests/fixtures/$case.env"
done
```

Fresh files go to `target/reference/$case-kraken/`. To update a golden, review
numerical changes first, copy its `.mod/.shd/.prt` here, trim trailing whitespace
from `.prt` lines, and update hashes below. Binary files are unmodified; `.prt`
CPU timings are nondeterministic, so the test reads only its modal table.
The test-only reader is `../../differential_reference.rs`. For broadband
regeneration commands, see [tools/README.md](../../../../../tools/README.md).
It compares all per-frequency record blocks and includes a later-frequency
corruption check; it never treats the first block as the entire file.

One comparator runs on committed files without Docker and fresh Fortran files
in CI. It checks counts, coordinates, frequency, printed and binary wavenumbers,
attenuation, phase/group speeds, unit-phase-aligned shapes **without amplitude
rescaling**, and every complex pressure. Tolerances: printed k `5e-10`,
shapes `1e-6`, pressure `2e-6`, group speed `0.005` (two decimal print digits).
Lossless binary complex32 wavenumbers must match exactly; with bottom loss,
the imaginary binary component has a `1e-10` absolute bound (measured max
`5.83e-11` on the independent 3 dB/wavelength fixture); the real component
still matches exactly. The imaginary part depends on first-mesh roots and
Fortran's complex-square-root rounding. Printed loss uses its `G10.2` half-last-digit precision.
The public attenuation is positive `-Im(k)`, whereas `.prt` prints signed `Im(k)`.

## KRAKENC cubic/analytic profile provenance

This slice reuses the existing **real/lossless** PCHIP/spline/analytic `Profile`,
not a complex-valued or lossy-water interpolation implementation. A-bottom
W attenuation and the existing FIELD/refinement/frequency semantics remain.
F/P tables remain N/C-only. Both mode solvers use the same analytic sampler,
retaining `munk.f90`'s f32 `eps` initialization and f32 `5000.0/N` step promotion.
No existing golden or tolerance is changed.

The five new fixtures are **derived**, not unmodified original pairs:

- `MunkLeakyPartialP/S`: relative to `MunkLeakyPartialLoss`, change the titles
  and N→P/S only, including `.flp` titles; keep seven knots, NG=800, RMax=0,
  0.8 W bottom loss, 30 modes (9 leaky) and 36 point-source pressures.
- `PekerisComplexSpline3`: derives from the real `PekerisSpline3` by changing
  title, `SVN`→`SVW`, NG 100→101, bottom W loss 0→0.25 and
  cHigh 1700→2000 m/s. Three nonuniform knots and RMax=1000 km remain.
  Coherent line-source `.flp` is copied from Pekeris. It has four modes
  (one leaky), nine pressures and reference meshes 1/2/4.
- `MunkAnalyticComplex`: derives from original `MunkAnalytic.env` by changing
  title, NG 0→2003, RMax 200→1000 km and modal receiver samples 501→11
  (0..5000 m endpoints). Source is still 1000 m; the separately derived
  coherent line-source `MunkAnalytic.flp` is reused unchanged (25 pressures).
  All 102 modes are compared; reference meshes are 1/2/4.
- `MunkLeakyPchipBroadband`: derives from the partial PCHIP case by changing
  title, NG 800→803, RMax 0→1000 km, adding sixth-slot B and frequencies
  75/50/62.5/50 Hz. FIELD changes only its title. Meshes 1/2/4 use intervals
  1204/2409/4818, 803/1606/3212 and 1003/2007/4015; repeated 50 Hz retains
  its own block. It has 45/30/37/30 modes and 36 pressures per block.

Three pinned runs per final fixture yield identical `.mod/.shd`. Binaries are
copied unchanged; `.prt` only trims trailing whitespace (timings are not an
identity requirement). Direct and actual CLI-HDF5 comparisons check all modes,
shapes, speeds, attenuation and pressures. Local pressure errors for P/S are
8.33e-9 each, three-point spline 2.99e-8, analytic 6.10e-9 and broadband
at most 7.46e-9. Numeric validation still rejects spline undershoot and
P/S coefficient overflow.

Two **unmodified original environments** are also run three times with
KRAKENC, with 102 modes/25 pressures each: `tests/Munk/MunkS.env` (S) and
`MunkAnalytic.env` (A), automatic NG and RMax=200 km (reference meshes 1/2).
MunkS was a **SCOOTER** fixture in upstream `runtests.m`; this is an environment
reuse, not SCOOTER support. Their identical original three-line `.flp` fails
in pinned FIELD (`Bad integer for item 1 in list input`); both receive the
separately derived coherent `MunkAnalytic.flp`, never a claim of original-pair
acceptance. Three reference `.mod/.shd` pairs are identical, and full direct /
actual CLI-HDF5 differential passes (local pressures 1.87e-9 / 3.73e-9).
Original binaries stay out of Git. Local manifests, source/compiler record
and original-pair rejection log are under `target/reference/profile-stage`.

The unmodified original **BroadBand/MunkK** remains accepted at 50/500 Hz
through **KRAKEN**. A local KRAKENC S-profile run matches 50 Hz (102 modes,
501,501 pressures), but 500 Hz exceeds its unchanged 300M root-work budget.
Reference generation for both frequencies is only smoke, not Rust acceptance.
An ignored fresh-CI CLI regression asserts exit 3 at frequency index 1,
retains an old output and removes scratch after 50 Hz succeeds. No partial
file, truncated reference modes or budget/tolerance increase is used.

## TabRefCoef input and resource provenance

`TabRefBrcN/C` and `TabRefIrcN/C` are **derived inputs**, not the original
TabRefCoef workflow. The water SSP endpoints and modal depths come from
`neggradC_brc/irc`; title, frequency 500→50 Hz, NG 1000→100 and N/C interpolation
are explicit changes. Their reduced `.flp` has ranges 0/0.5/1 km, receivers
0/50/100 m and zero offsets. N variants use a line source at 0 m (also endpoint
extension); C variants use a point source at 10 m. All retain vacuum top,
RMax=0 and blank restarts. Their tables are **constructed**, not generated by
BOUNCE or thinned copies of its outputs:

- BRC: 0/45/90 degrees, magnitude 0.8 and unwrapped phase 170/190/210 degrees.
- IRC: real k² 0.01/0.03/0.05, powers 0/10/20; stored f is
  `(0.01+0.01i) * 10^-power`, stored g is `1 * 10^-power`.

Three pinned runs of each final fixture yield identical `.mod/.shd`. Raw
binaries are copied unchanged; `.prt` only removes trailing whitespace. The
same committed/fresh comparator checks every mode, phase-aligned shape,
printed/binary wave number, attenuation, phase/group speed and pressure. Local
maximum pressure errors for BRC N/C are 0 / 7.46e-9, and IRC N/C are
0 / 1.67e-8, at the existing 2e-6 pressure and 1e-6 shape tolerances.
Unit regressions separately lock IRC polynomial/scaling/domain semantics, BRC
unwrapped phase/f32 brackets, and the pinned GNU real-component grouping.

For the **unmodified original** `neggradC_geo/brc/irc` `.env/.flp`, upstream
`runtests.m` selects KRAKENC (real KRAKEN does not support these tables).
The directory contains **no `.brc/.irc`**. `tools/reference/prepare-tabref.sh`
copies the original bytes and uses rebuilt pinned BOUNCE to generate resources
from original `neggradB.env`. Docker explicitly deletes archived `bounce.exe`
and `bounce.o` before compiling with the recorded flags. Three independent
runs generate identical tables and `.mod/.shd`; manifests and build information
remain under `target/reference/TabRefCoef`. Reference smoke alone is not Rust
acceptance: fresh CI compares the full Rust result and actual CLI HDF5 readback.
Original binaries/tables are not committed. The original `.env` samples
1..100 m; original `.flp` requests 0..100 m. Neither input is changed to avoid
FIELD endpoint extension. Each result is compared to its own reference; BRC,
IRC and geo need not agree. Local pressure errors are respectively 2.75e-7,
5.96e-8 and 5.96e-8. Tolerances and numerical budgets are unchanged.
Neither repeatability nor these comparisons prove every mathematical root was
found; table seeding retains the fixed reference's branch-sensitive search.
